examDifficulty.heading: Is the Education Cloud Consultant Exam Hard?
examDifficulty.summary: The Education Cloud Consultant exam is moderately to significantly difficult. It covers the Education Data Architecture (EDA), student lifecycle management, advising workflows, and integration with SIS/LMS systems. Candidates need both Salesforce platform skills and understanding of higher education processes.
bullets: ~65% passing score — roughly 39 correct answers needed.
EDA data model is central — you must understand affiliations, course connections, program plans, and how EDA replaces the standard account/contact model.
Cross-functional knowledge required — questions span admissions, advising, advancement (fundraising), and IT integration scenarios.
examDifficulty.passRateGuidance: Score 75%+ on practice exams and ensure you can diagram the EDA object model before booking. Prior experience with a higher education Salesforce implementation or familiarity with university admissions and advising processes is strongly recommended.

examFormat.heading: Education Cloud Consultant Exam Format Explained
examFormat.intro: The exam is proctored online or in-person. Here is the format:
examFormat.scenarioPercent: About 50-60% of questions are scenario-based. Common patterns include designing an admissions pipeline for a university, configuring Student Success Hub alerts for at-risk students, and selecting the right integration approach for SIS data.
bestWayToPass: Master the EDA data model: Know accounts (institutions, departments, households), contacts (students, faculty), affiliations, course connections, and program plans inside and out.
Understand the student lifecycle: Study how prospects move through recruitment, admissions, enrollment, retention, and alumni engagement in Education Cloud.
Learn Student Success Hub: Know how to configure alerts, advising appointments, success plans, and case management for student support workflows.
Study integration patterns: Understand how Education Cloud integrates with SIS (Banner, PeopleSoft) and LMS (Canvas, Blackboard) systems, and which system is the record of truth for academic data.

certificationCard.description: This exam tests configuring Education Data Architecture (EDA), student lifecycle management, and advising workflows for schools and universities. Expect questions on admissions pipelines, course enrollment, and SIS/LMS integration.

keyConcepts.h2: Education Cloud Consultant: Key Concepts for the Exam

blocks.heading: EDA: Education Data Architecture Core Objects
blocks.body: Education Cloud is built on EDA (Education Data Architecture), an open-source data model from Salesforce.org. Core objects: Contact (represents students, faculty, and staff), Account (educational institution, department, household), Term (academic period — semester, quarter), Course (a subject offering), Course Connection (a student's enrollment in a course for a term), Program Plan (degree plan with requirements). Affiliations connect contacts to multiple accounts (a student affiliated with their major department, a dormitory, and the institution). The consultant configures EDA to match the institution's academic structure.

blocks.heading: Student Success Hub: Alerts, Cases, and Appointments
blocks.body: Student Success Hub (SSH) is the advising and student success platform in Education Cloud. Key features: Alerts flag students at risk (attendance drops, grade thresholds, hold flags). Cases manage student issues requiring follow-up. Appointments enable students to book advising sessions (integrates with calendar systems). Success Plans create personalised student action plans with milestones. Advising notes capture interaction history. The consultant configures SSH to match the institution's student success model — defining which alert triggers are enabled, how cases are routed to advisors, and what appointment types are available.

blocks.heading: Recruiting and Admissions
blocks.body: Education Cloud supports the full student recruitment lifecycle. Inquiry captures prospective student interest. Application tracks the admissions application and review process. Prospect/Lead management assigns recruiter territories and tracks outreach activities. Program Interest records which academic programmes a prospect is interested in. The consultant configures the recruiting pipeline stages, application workflow (application submitted → under review → decision made → enrolled), and integration with external application management systems (Common App, Slate).

blocks.heading: Experience Cloud for Students and Faculty
blocks.body: Education Cloud leverages Experience Cloud to build self-service portals for students and faculty. Student portals: course registration, financial aid status, advising appointment booking, campus services requests. Faculty portals: course rosters, grade submission, office hours management. Community engagement: peer discussion groups, club pages, alumni networks. The consultant configures the Experience Cloud site using appropriate templates, sharing settings (Sharing Sets for student record access), and **Knowledge articles** for self-service resolution of common questions.

blocks.heading: Integration with SIS and LMS Systems
blocks.body: Educational institutions typically have existing systems of record: SIS (Student Information System — PeopleSoft, Banner, Colleague) for official academic records and LMS (Learning Management System — Canvas, Blackboard, Moodle) for course delivery. Education Cloud Salesforce serves as the engagement CRM layer — not the system of record for academic transcripts. Integration patterns: SIS sync pushes enrollment status, grades, and course connections into Salesforce. LMS integration surfaces course activity data for success coaching. The consultant designs the integration architecture — what data flows in each direction, at what frequency, and which system is the golden record for each data element.

scenarioTips.h2: How to Pass the Salesforce Education Cloud Consultant Exam
scenarioTips.intro: The Education Cloud Consultant exam tests implementation of Salesforce for higher education institutions. Focus on the Education Data Architecture (EDA), student lifecycle management, and how Education Cloud extends standard Salesforce.

blocks.heading: Education Data Architecture (EDA)
blocks.body: EDA replaces the standard Account/Contact model with an education-specific model: Accounts as educational institutions, Contacts as students/faculty, and Affiliations linking them. Know how EDA's Household and Administrative account types differ.

blocks.heading: Student Lifecycle Management
blocks.body: Understand how Admissions Connect, Student Success Hub, and Recruitment and Admissions features map to the student journey from prospect through alumni. Know which features are in Education Cloud vs. standard Salesforce.

blocks.heading: Program Enrollment & Course Management
blocks.body: Know the EDA objects: Programs, Courses, Course Offerings, and Course Enrollments. Understand how students enroll in course offerings and how academic records are maintained.

blocks.heading: Advisor & Success Hub Configuration
blocks.body: Know how to configure the Success Hub for advisors with student alerts, appointments, and care plans. Understand how Advisor Link enables student-initiated advising appointments.

blocks.heading: Reporting for Education
blocks.body: Understand common education reporting needs: enrollment funnels, retention rates, advising caseloads, and alumni engagement. Know how to build reports using EDA-specific report types.
